A LITTLE CONTEXT

How this JSON comparison works

Paste a document on each side, or open local files, and select Compare JSON. The result follows field names and array indexes rather than matching text lines. Differences show a path, a change type and the value on each side. No changes are applied to either input.

Object keys: unordered · Arrays: ordered · Numbers: exact decimal values

References: RFC 6901: JSON Pointer · RFC 8259: JSON

Good to know

Does rearranging object keys count as a change?

No. {"a":1,"b":2} and {"b":2,"a":1} compare equal. String escape spellings that decode to the same valid string also compare equal. Whitespace and object member display order are ignored; the tool separately reports when the source texts differ.

Does array order matter?

Yes. Arrays compare by zero-based index. Moving a value may appear as several changed indexes. Appended values are added; removed trailing values are removed. This is not a move detector or an unordered collection matcher.

Are large numbers rounded before comparison?

No. Number source tokens are compared as exact base-10 values without converting to JavaScript Number. 1, 1.0 and 10e-1 match. 9007199254740992 and 9007199254740993 differ. -0 and 0 match by this tool’s policy. Number tokens are limited to 4,096 characters; exponents are normalized without expanding zeros.

How are missing fields, null and types represented?

A missing field is added or removed; it is not treated as null. JSON null differs from the string "null", and number 1 differs from string "1". If a value changes type, the report shows that value at its path rather than guessing a conversion.

What do /, ~0 and ~1 mean in a path?

Paths follow JSON Pointer escaping: ~ becomes ~0 and / inside a key becomes ~1. Array positions are decimal indexes. The empty pointer refers to the root and is displayed as (root); / by itself refers to an object key that is an empty string. A pointer identifies a value, not an executable command.

What does the report include, and what are the limits?

Each document is limited to 1,000,000 UTF-16 code units, files to 2 MB, nesting to 80 levels, and values plus fields to 50,000. Duplicate keys, malformed syntax and unpaired Unicode surrogates are rejected. At most 200 differences and 500,000 serialized preview characters are listed, and a visible notice marks incomplete reports. A reported difference path must fit within 4,096 characters. Individual values are previewed up to 500 characters. Downloaded JSON contains the same previews and truncation flags; it is not a full replacement document or JSON Patch.

PRACTICAL REFERENCE

Read a difference without losing its meaning

Use the change type and value type together. The same text can have a different meaning when it belongs to a JSON string.

LeftRightResult
{"a":1,"b":2}{"b":2,"a":1.0}Same values; different source text
{}{"note":null}Added at /note
{"n":1}{"n":"1"}Changed type at /n
["red","blue"]["blue","red"]Changed at /0 and /1
{"a/b":{"~key":1}}{"a/b":{"~key":2}}Changed at /a~1b/~0key

This tool compares valid JSON values; it does not validate them against a JSON Schema, infer a primary key, merge changes, or compare JSON Lines files. Use JSON format and validate to inspect one document, JSON unescape for a quoted string containing JSON, and YAML to JSON for supported YAML input.
